latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Pathogenic antibodies against neuronal surface or synaptic proteins create reversible synaptic dysfunction rather than primary pathogen replication or abscess formation.
Compartmental humoral inflammation in serum, CSF, or both sustains antibody production and mild lymphocytic CSF inflammation in many autoimmune encephalitis presentations.
Hippocampal, amygdalar, insular, and frontolimbic network dysfunction produces subacute memory loss, behavioral change, psychiatric symptoms, and limbic MRI or EEG abnormalities.
Autoimmune synaptic disruption and limbic inflammation lower seizure threshold, causing focal seizures, generalized seizures, FBDS, or refractory status epilepticus depending on antibody context.
NMDAR antibody activity preferentially drives psychosis, agitation, orofacial dyskinesia, catatonia-like encephalopathy, autonomic instability, and central hypoventilation.
LGI1-predominant disease causes frequent brief faciobrachial dystonic seizures, limbic memory impairment, medial temporal MRI signal, and ADH-mediated hyponatremia.
Ovarian teratoma, thymoma, small-cell lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, and other tumors can maintain antigenic stimulation and relapse risk until tumor-directed source control is achieved.
Mild to moderate lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis and protein leak support CNS immune inflammation, but normal CSF does not exclude autoimmune encephalitis.
Severe autoimmune encephalitis, especially NMDAR phenotype, can cause autonomic instability, hypoventilation, aspiration risk, ICU need, and death independent of systemic sepsis.
Delayed immunotherapy, delayed tumor removal, refractory seizures, and prolonged ICU course increase residual memory loss, epilepsy, relapse, disability, and mortality hazard.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Neuronal surface antibodies disturb synaptic receptors and adhesion complexes in limbic networks.
Ongoing B-cell and plasma-cell activity sustains antibody burden.
Tumor or teratoma antigen expression can maintain autoimmune priming.
Serum or CSF neuronal surface antibody detection reflects active antibody biology when tested.
Limbic and cortical network dysfunction causes encephalopathy, confusion, or coma.
Behavioral disturbance and agitation are core clinical manifestations.
Hippocampal dysfunction produces short-term memory impairment and amnesia.
Medial temporal and limbic MRI abnormalities are common in limbic autoimmune encephalitis, though MRI can be normal.
Temporal lobe FLAIR signal tracks limbic inflammation or edema in many antibody contexts.
Bilateral limbic involvement supports autoimmune mimics more than classic unilateral necrotizing HSV, while not being required.
Seizures are common across NMDAR, LGI1, GABAB, GABAA, AMPAR, and related autoimmune encephalitides.
Temporal or frontal-temporal epileptiform activity can accompany limbic autoimmune seizures.
EEG often shows nonspecific diffuse or focal slowing even without captured epileptiform activity.
Severe GABAA, GABAB, NMDAR, and seronegative cases can develop refractory status epilepticus.
NMDAR phenotype frequently begins with psychiatric symptoms.
Orofacial dyskinesias are characteristic but not required for NMDAR autoimmune encephalitis.
Severe NMDAR disease can cause central hypoventilation and ventilator dependence.
Catatonia-like decreased responsiveness and coma occur in severe NMDAR phenotype.
Extreme delta brush is a supportive EEG pattern in anti-NMDAR encephalitis when present.
FBDS is highly characteristic of LGI1 autoimmune encephalitis.
LGI1 disease is commonly associated with SIADH-like hyponatremia.
Low serum osmolality with concentrated urine and high urine sodium suggests SIADH physiology in LGI1 cases.
CSF lymphocytic inflammation can be present but may be absent in LGI1 and some NMDAR cases.
When CSF is inflammatory, pleocytosis is usually mild to moderate and often lymphocytic.
Blood-CSF barrier leak may mildly raise CSF protein.
Tumor context raises the paraneoplastic branch of autoimmune encephalitis.
Ovarian teratoma is a major antigenic driver in anti-NMDAR encephalitis in young women.
Persistent tumor antigenic drive makes oncologic source control important when a tumor is found.
Autonomic dysregulation is a core severity axis in severe NMDAR and related autoimmune encephalitis.
Central hypoventilation and airway failure drive ICU need and mortality.
Seizures, dyskinesia, decreased responsiveness, and ventilation raise aspiration risk.
Delayed disease control increases residual cognitive deficits and epilepsy.
Incomplete immune control or unresected tumor increases relapse risk.
Deaths are usually mediated by autonomic, respiratory, seizure, ICU, or neurologic complications rather than a separate death manifold.
Long untreated disease and refractory status raise mortality and severe disability risk.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: CSF cellular inflammation and protein leak often travel together in autoimmune encephalitis.
Autoimmune CSF pleocytosis is more often lymphocytic than neutrophilic.

axis_couplings.conditionality: strongest in LGI1/SIADH physiology and severe hyponatremia
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Lower sodium increases seizure susceptibility and can amplify autoimmune seizure burden.
Hippocampal/limbic imaging abnormalities often correspond to memory impairment.
Active seizures can escalate into refractory status epilepticus in severe antibody-mediated encephalitis.
Central hypoventilation directly raises airway and ventilatory failure risk.
Respiratory failure is a major pathway to death in severe autoimmune encephalitis.
Refractory status epilepticus increases downstream disability and persistent epilepsy.
Autonomic instability can cause cardiovascular collapse and ICU mortality.

axis_couplings.conditionality: applies when tumor is present and unresected or incompletely treated
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Persistent tumor antigenic drive increases relapse and refractory disease risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: High-dose steroids can worsen untreated HSV, bacterial meningitis, abscess, TB, or fungal infection if infection has not been addressed.
Steroids can worsen hyperglycemia, psychiatric agitation, gastrointestinal bleeding, and infection risk.

side_effects.interpretation: Steroids increase infection, metabolic, psychiatric, and gastrointestinal toxicity risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Fast broad immune-inflammatory vector that can reduce barrier inflammation and clinical deterioration once CNS infection is being covered or excluded.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal dysfunction, thrombosis risk, hyperviscosity, and volume sensitivity can constrain IVIG.

side_effects.interpretation: IVIG toxicity is context dependent and usually lower than prolonged cytotoxic therapy.

treatments.context_specific_role: Antibody-neutralizing and immune-modulating vector often paired with steroids or plasma exchange.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hemodynamic instability, access problems, bleeding risk, or low-resource settings can prevent adequate exchange.

side_effects.interpretation: Procedural hypotension, line infection, bleeding, and electrolyte shifts can occur.

treatments.context_specific_role: Fast antibody-removal vector, especially useful when seizures or encephalopathy worsen despite steroids and IVIG.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Active severe infection, profound hypogammaglobulinemia, or hepatitis B reactivation risk can limit B-cell depletion.

side_effects.interpretation: B-cell depletion raises infection and reactivation risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Durable B-cell vector for refractory or relapsing autoimmune encephalitis.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Cytopenia, infertility, bladder toxicity, and infection risk are important constraints.

side_effects.interpretation: Cytotoxic toxicity can be substantial and context dependent.

treatments.context_specific_role: Escalation vector for severe refractory disease when benefits outweigh cytotoxic toxicity.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: When tumor antigenic drive is present, removal can markedly accelerate immune control and reduce relapse.

side_effects.interpretation: Surgical risks vary by tumor site, reproductive context, and critical illness severity.

treatments.context_specific_role: Tumor-source vector; not applicable when no tumor is present or likely.
Symptomatic seizure-control vector that does not remove antibody-driven disease by itself.

side_effects.interpretation: Critical illness and ventilation can add secondary pneumonia risk even while reducing immediate respiratory mortality.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supportive state-push vector for severe autonomic or respiratory failure; does not treat the autoimmune source.

female_age_12_to_45_or_ovarian_teratoma.trajectory_modulation: Raises probability of NMDAR phenotype, orofacial dyskinesia, psychiatric prodrome, autonomic instability, and benefit from tumor-source control when teratoma is present.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Young women are enriched for anti-NMDAR disease.
Ovarian teratoma is a major trigger in this demographic.

older_male_with_limbic_seizures_or_fbds.trajectory_modulation: Raises LGI1-like trajectory with FBDS, medial temporal MRI signal, mild or normal CSF, and hyponatremia.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: FBDS is strongly associated with LGI1.

known_or_occult_solid_tumor.trajectory_modulation: Raises paraneoplastic branch probability, treatment dependence on tumor control, and relapse risk if tumor remains active.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: GABAB, AMPAR, CASPR2, and some NMDAR contexts can be paraneoplastic.
Tumor-source control matters when tumor antigen drives disease.

recent_hsv_or_other_cns_viral_encephalit.trajectory_modulation: Can produce delayed autoimmune encephalitis after infectious encephalitis, requiring distinction between viral replication and autoimmune rebound.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Recent HSV makes active viral relapse and autoimmune sequela both plausible until virology is checked.

delayed_or_incomplete_disease_control.trajectory_modulation: Does not define diagnosis but increases status epilepticus, ICU course, disability, relapse, and mortality hazards.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Long untreated active disease accumulates neuronal injury.

active_infection_frailty_pregnancy_renal.trajectory_modulation: Does not make autoimmune encephalitis more likely by itself, but reshapes feasible immunotherapy bundles and toxicity hazard.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Host context affects steroid, IVIG, plasma exchange, rituximab, and cyclophosphamide safety.

supportive_care: Cover or rapidly exclude HSV encephalitis, bacterial meningitis, brain abscess, VZV CNS disease, toxic-metabolic delirium, primary psychiatric disease, CNS lupus, Behcet, sarcoidosis, and malignancy before committing to isolated autoimmune treatment.
Obtain CSF cell count, protein, glucose with serum glucose, oligoclonal bands or IgG index when available, infectious PCR/culture, and paired serum/CSF autoimmune encephalitis antibody testing.
Use brain MRI with FLAIR/DWI/contrast and EEG; repeat MRI or EEG if the first study is normal but the clinical syndrome remains strongly encephalitic.

Screen for tumor context guided by age, sex, antibody phenotype, and imaging: pelvic ultrasound/MRI for teratoma, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, testicular or thymic evaluation, and PET when clinically needed.

Treat seizures, status epilepticus, agitation, dysautonomia, aspiration risk, nutrition, venous thromboembolism risk, pressure injury risk, sleep-wake disruption, and rehabilitation needs as state axes alongside immunotherapy.
Reassess for relapse, residual memory impairment, psychiatric recovery, epilepsy, and treatment complications after acute stabilization.
distillation_quality_notes: Disease name is pure first-layer Autoimmune encephalitis; antibody subtype and tumor context are represented as axes, mechanisms, risk modifiers, and treatment modifiers.

HSV encephalitis, VZV encephalitis, viral or bacterial meningitis, brain abscess, CNS lupus/SLE flare, neuro-Behcet, neurosarcoidosis, toxic-metabolic delirium, and primary psychiatric disease are not included in the disease name.
Antibody positivity and tumor pathology can be stored as confirmatory/post-workup evidence in cases; presentation-only ranking should rely on clinical, CSF, MRI, EEG, and context axes.
